paper_id: Xiao et al. - 2005 - Dynamic Layer Management in Superpeer Architectures
title: Dynamic Layer Management in Superpeer Architectures
venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
motivation: Superpeer P2P systems lack layer management; transient/low-capacity peers act as superpeers and size ratio is uncontrolled
problem_framing: Three open problems: optimal leaf-to-super ratio, ratio maintenance, and peer selection for superlayer
key_insight: Optimal ratio = sqrt((B-C)/A)-1 by minimizing weighted workload combining superpeer load and network-wide load
method_signature: Workload model (connection+query+relay) + distributed DLM with scaled capacity/age comparisons
evaluation_criteria: Layer size ratio stability, superpeer avg capacity/age, weighted workload minimization vs theoretical optimum
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Cannot minimize superpeer workload and network workload simultaneously; trade-off is fundamental
evidence_for_taste: impossible to minimize these two workloads
there is a trade-off between these two workloads
Unfortunately, these two goals are not always compatible
the ratio of PAO to NLCO is trivial
thinking_moves: 把全局优化问题分解为可独立计算的最优参数
引入对数比例mu=log(l_nn/k_l)作为失衡标志
用比例控制调节规模参数X_capa和X_age
先建模证明最坏/最优情况界再仿真验证
